about: CHAIN amber_road (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/amber_road.md; words Data/writing/chain_amber_road.json). Amber from the Ests at Truso, as Wulfstan saw them about 890 (Old English Orosius; texts_793.json wulfstan): a king in every fort, mares' milk for the rich and mead for the poor and no ale at all, the dead kept cold in their houses for months, their goods laid out along a mile and ridden for, every stranger who dies there burned. Fourteen cards. The body of the chain is open while Truso stands in ports_793.json (to 850); the last card is Wulfstan himself at Sliesthorp, 880 to 899, for the heir. Step flags ch_amber_road_1 .. _9; endings ch_amber_road_end_rider (the stranger who rode), ch_amber_road_end_guest (what happened: a guest who learned the trade), ch_amber_road_end_ale (history changed: changed_ests_brew_ale), ch_amber_road_end_shut (history changed: changed_ests_bar_strangers). Every option's note names its outcome text. Spoken lines call people by what they are (the Dane, the steward, the brew-wife) because the engine forges the names. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, one of the two starts (drawn at Ripa or Sliesthorp before 846). A bead-maker's raw amber has come through three hands; he says where it comes from and shows how it is told from resin and glass. Sources: amber worked into beads at Ribe and Hedeby (goods_793.json amber; economy/furs_amber_ivory_slaves.md: workshop waste at Ripa, Sliesthorp, Truso); the seven days and the Wends to starboard are Wulfstan's (texts_793.json wulfstan); that the Ests wonder at the price is Tacitus, Germania 45 (from memory (?)). The three tests (it draws chaff when rubbed, floats in brine, is warm on the lip) are craft knowledge with no source of the period (?). The bead-maker Toki is invented (a Danish name of the rune stones). Sets ch_amber_road_1 and, by two of the three options, ch_amber_road_rub.

cards.note: Step 2, the other start (drawn at Truso on any call before 850; it does not need step 1). The king of the fort is dead and lies in his house; his store is shut until he is burned; the stranger is offered a drink. Source, all Wulfstan (texts_793.json wulfstan; our rendering): a king in every fort; the king and the richest men drink mares' milk, the poor and the slaves mead; no ale is brewed among the Ests, but there is mead enough; the dead lie unburnt a month, sometimes two, kings and great men longer, sometimes half a year, and all that while there is drinking and play. Danes with scales at the lake market: spine.md, thread 7, Truso. That the king's store is shut during the wake while gleanings are sold on the beach is ours (?). The host Ketil (a Dane settled at Truso) and the steward Nalube (a Prussian name recorded only in the 13th century (?)) are invented. Sets ch_amber_road_2 and one of ch_amber_road_milk, ch_amber_road_low_bench, ch_amber_road_ale_tasted.

cards.note: Step 3 (scheduled by step 2; three days on). The dead king in his house, and the kin that can make cold. Source: Wulfstan (our rendering): there is among the Ests a kin that can make cold, and so the dead lie long and do not rot; set two vessels of ale or water before them and they bring it about that both are frozen over, summer or winter. How it was done is not recorded: the pit of winter ice under the bench is a guess (?), and the card leaves half of it untold. The cold-wife Drua (a late Prussian woman's name (?)) is invented. Sets ch_amber_road_3; ch_amber_road_gift, or ch_amber_road_cold_known.

cards.note: Step 4, a turn (scheduled by step 3; four days on). A woman sells gleanings on the beach in three wet heaps at one price; the Dane weighs and says nothing. The trade that has to be learned. Sources: Tacitus, Germania 45: the Aestii gather amber, bring it unworked and take their price with wonder (from memory (?)); it is turned round here: by 800 they know to the grain what a stranger does not. Amber gathered on the west shore (Witland, Samland) after the autumn storms: goods_793.json amber. Pine resin boiled hard and yellow glass passed as amber are our guess at the frauds (?). The seller Nameda (a late Prussian woman's name (?)) is invented. Sets ch_amber_road_4; pays four or five sacks to the careful (about 120 to 150 d for 30 to 45 d).

cards.note: Step 5 (scheduled by step 4; four days on). A baptised Frisian has died in the guest house and his son has promised him earth. Source: Wulfstan (our rendering): it is a custom among the Ests that a man of every tongue shall be burned, and if a bone is found unburnt they must make great atonement for it. Who pays the atonement is not said: that it falls on the house that kept the dead man is ours (?). There is no church nearer than Saxony before the 850s (Anskar's churches at Sliesthorp and Ripa: realms/denmark.md), so Christian ground here is a grave in the sand of the spit with a cross of driftwood. The dead man Wigbod (Wig- + -bod) and his son Wigmar (Wig- + -mar), Frisians of the Weser mouth, are invented. Sets ch_amber_road_5; ch_amber_road_body_out, ch_amber_road_burned or ch_amber_road_atoned. The riddle of ice is Symphosius 10 (riddles_793.json).

cards.note: Step 6 (scheduled by step 5; three days on). The day of the burning is named and the riding explained; the stranger says what he will bring. Source: Wulfstan (our rendering): on the day they carry him to the pyre they divide what is left of his goods into five or six parts, sometimes more; they lay the largest about a mile from the fort, then the next, and the least nearest the fort; all the men with the swiftest horses in the land gather five or six miles from the goods and ride for them, and the first takes the largest part, and each keeps what he reaches; for that reason swift horses are very dear there; most of the wealth is spent in the long lying and in what is laid by the road, which strangers ride for and take. That a stranger may ride is in the text itself. The heir Gedune, the dead king's brother (a late Prussian name (?)), is invented. Sets ch_amber_road_6 and schedules the race seventy days on; ch_amber_road_horse_errand or ch_amber_road_brew_errand.

cards.note: Step 7, the errand in the west (drawn at Sliesthorp or Ripa between step 6 and the race; it comes again after twelve days if he said 'not now'). A Jute with one fast grey horse, and a brew-wife who wants a share and not a wage. Sources: swift horses very dear among the Ests (Wulfstan); brewing is women's household work (npc_roles_793.json alewife); horses carried in ships are shown later on the Bayeux embroidery, about 1070 (LATER), and the Danes' horses crossed to England in 892 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 893 for 892, 'with horses and all'). The horse costs twice the table's 120 d. The dealer Asbjorn and the brew-wife Tofa are invented (Danish names of the rune stones). Sets ch_amber_road_7; ch_amber_road_grey, ch_amber_road_brew.

Source: Wulfstan, as at step 6; and: when his goods are all spent so, they carry him out and burn him with his weapons and clothes. A stranger riding is in the text; a stranger winning is not said, and nothing says he could not. The danger warns first: the Dane says what a thief at a burning pays, and who pays with him. cards.note: ENDING: the stranger who rode (scheduled by step 9, the morning after the burning). The hard road: a horse bought dear, carried seven days in an open boat, and ridden. Source: Wulfstan: strangers ride for the goods and take them; each keeps what he reaches; so swift horses are very dear there. Finale 620 to about 2,000 d in goods and silver at the table's values. Grand rewards: unlock_title_est_guest_friend (the new king's hand: his house's boat is a guest's boat at this fort; guest-friendship across the sea is the north's own way, Havamal 41-44) and, for the winner, unlock_heirloom_burning_bridle (the dead king's bridle from the far heap) or unlock_plot_truso (ground by the lake; the finds at Janow Pomorski show strangers' houses on the shore (?)). Sets ch_amber_road_end_rider.

cards.note: ENDING: history changed (scheduled by step 9, the morning after the burning). Wulfstan, about 890: 'no ale is brewed among the Ests, but there is mead enough' (our rendering). Here a brew-wife from the west has served ale at a king's burning and the new king wants a brewhouse: ale among the Ests two lifetimes or more before anyone records it. The Old Prussian word alu is glossed 'mead' and piwis 'beer' in the Elbing vocabulary of about 1400 (from memory (?); LATER): the card lets them call the new drink by an old word. Sets ch_amber_road_end_ale and changed_ests_brew_ale. Finale 860 to 1,100 d in amber and silver, with malt dear at Truso for a year. Grand rewards: unlock_work_truso_brewhouse with unlock_factor_truso (the brew-wife keeps his goods), or unlock_charter_truso (the king's peace: no gift owed at this fort), or unlock_title_est_guest_friend.

cards.note: ENDING: what happened (scheduled by step 9, the morning after the burning). Strangers traded on the Ests' lake as guests, weighed amber against silver and went home; the Ests kept their kings, their milk, their mead and their fire, and were still as Wulfstan found them two generations on. The king's store opens the day after the burning (ours (?)); a guest who sat out the wake is paid what he won at the wake's play (Wulfstan: drinking and play all the while the dead man lies within) and is weighed first. Finale 600 to 680 d in amber with silver. Grand rewards, one of: unlock_factor_truso (the Dane keeps his goods), unlock_pilot_estmere (the bars of the Vistula's mouth, the Estmere fifteen miles broad and the Ilfing up to the lake: Wulfstan's own way in), unlock_partner_wigmar (the dead Frisian's son, if his father was got to earth or atoned for), unlock_upgrade_ice_chest (a chest of the cold-wife's packing, if he was shown the cold: how it was done is a guess (?)). Sets ch_amber_road_end_guest.

cards.note: ENDING: history changed for the worse (scheduled by the theft at step 9; at Sliesthorp ten days on). He robbed the heaps at a king's burning. The Dane who answered for him has paid the atonement with his house, and the Ests hold strangers to the beach: no stranger in the fort, at a wake or on a horse. Wulfstan about 890 saw strangers ride; here he will not be let see it. Sources: the 'great atonement' is Wulfstan's word for a bone left unburnt; that a host answers for his guest is the north's and Kent's rule (npc_roles_793.json host); the rest is ours. Sets ch_amber_road_end_shut and, unless he makes amends, changed_ests_bar_strangers; ch_amber_road_truso_shut is the cost that lasts. Finale 600 to 640 d. Grand rewards: unlock_factor_sliesthorp (a bead-maker who does not ask), or unlock_pilot_curonia (the Curonians' amber shore north of the Neman, as far as Grobin), or, by the costly road, the Dane restored and unlock_factor_truso.

cards.intention: A Gotland boat came in from the east two days before you. By the time you make fast, the bead-makers' row knows what a Frisian did at a king's burning on the Ests' lake.

options.label: Sell the bead-maker what you know and what you took, and let him do your buying in the east
options.note: outcome: chain_amber_road.end_shut.out_sell (620 d for the lake's prices, its seasons and the loot's worth; a man at Sliesthorp who works his amber from wherever it comes)

options.label: Pay the Gotlander to show you the Curonians' shore: they have amber too, and have not heard of you
options.note: outcome: chain_amber_road.end_shut.out_curonians (600 d from the bead-makers' row, less nothing: the Gotlander takes his pay in what you know of Truso)

options.label: Send the whole atonement east with the Gotlander, and more, in the Dane's name
options.note: outcome: chain_amber_road.end_shut.out_amends (300 d: the Dane has his house again and holds his goods, the fort lets strangers ride again, and he himself is never asked inside the palisade)

memory.sell: sold what he took from a burning
memory.curonians: asked the way to the Curonians

cards.note: AFTERWORD, for the heir (drawn at Sliesthorp, 880 to 899; open to every house, with more to say to one that knows the lake). Wulfstan (cast.wulfstan; real; of the English by his name) is back from Truso and tells his voyage as he will tell it to King Alfred. Source: the Old English Orosius, about 890 (texts_793.json wulfstan; chronicle_793.json 890-ohthere-wulfstan); the lines are our rendering of his words. What the house did two generations before changes two of his sentences: 'no ale is brewed among the Ests' (changed_ests_brew_ale) and 'strangers ride for it and take it' (changed_ests_bar_strangers). The clerk who writes it down for him at Sliesthorp and lets a leaf be copied is invented (?): the account was written at Alfred's court. NEEDS: ports_793.json ends Truso in 850, which Wulfstan's own voyage contradicts. Sets ch_amber_road_wulfstan.
cards.when: moored and port.id = sliesthorp and year >= 880 and year < 900 and not flag.ch_amber_road_wulfstan

clerk.note: an English clerk in his company; invented, unnamed

cards.title: Lands to port, lands to starboard
cards.intention: An Englishman is back from the Ests' lake with a string of rough amber round his wrist and a great deal to say. He means to tell all of it to his king. First he wants to tell it to someone who can say whether he has it right.

options.label: Hear him through, and put him right where your house knows better
options.note: outcome: chain_amber_road.x_wulfstan.out_hear (the afternoon; the clerk's leaf goes in the chest)

options.label: Tell him what your house knows of the bars at the river mouth, for a price
options.note: outcome: chain_amber_road.x_wulfstan.out_sell (120 d and the leaf)

options.label: Let him talk, and tell him nothing: the road is your house's
options.note: outcome: chain_amber_road.x_wulfstan.out_silent (nothing given, nothing got; he sails for England all the same)

memory.sell: sold him the bars of the river mouth
